failure_summary.description: Entity codes and selector fields were left out of the optional list: CarrierCode=UA from 'United Airlines (UA)', `by`=Group Name for K-POP, and pageSize in the news task.
Values were emitted in the wrong case or form. Gold used lowercase `english`, `bellman`, `uk` and `in`, and the postal code `WA` for 'Washington state'.

Email clauses were dropped or mis-stacked. In email:130 the 'techvision.com classified as disposable' clause lost its MailCheck: Domain call while a redundant disposable-email call was added. In email:98 'comprehensive checks on email and domain' got 3 of 6 calls. In email:7 the valid/deliverability clauses were routed to the wrong verifiers.
'Search for travel locations in London' was routed to Priceline 'Search flights locations' instead of 'Search hotels locations', whose description says 'travel locations'.
news:101 gold contains unrelated tools (Arabic news, German police, dev-to), so it is not chased.

patch.reasoning: All 8 trajectories parsed cleanly, so the format section stays untouched; edits to it caused the earlier rejects. The remaining losses are content-level: missing optionals for codes and selector fields, value case or form, under-calling or mis-stacking email clauses, and one sibling mismatch. The four edits each merge into or sit beside an existing rule instead of adding a new section. One edit gives a count-style rule for email 'comprehensive' versus 'valid AND disposable' with an explicit boundary. One turns the `by` bullet into an every-code-needs-a-field audit with a flight example. One adds a wording-match example for generic 'travel locations'. One adds a value-case exception for music and state tools.

edits.target: 'Comprehensive checks on an email and its domain' = an email-level validator with the full address plus domain-level tools with the bare domain (`MailCheck: Domain`, `fast Email verifier: Role Account`, `fast Email verifier: disposable Domain and Suggest Domain`).
edits.content: 'Comprehensive / thorough checks on an email and its domain' (or 'run checks on both the email and the domain') = every email-level validator that covers valid/disposable (`Easy Email Validation: Validate Email`, `Email Validation_v3: Validate_Email`) with the full address PLUS every domain-level tool in the list with the bare domain, one call each (`MailCheck: Domain`, `fast Email verifier: Role Account`, `fast Email verifier: disposable Domain and Suggest Domain`). That is about 5 calls, plus 1 for a fake-email clause (`Email API: Get Fake Email Address`). BOUNDARY: a plain 'valid AND disposable' on one address (no 'comprehensive') is ONE call to a tool whose description names both (`Alpha Email Verification: Email Checker`, `Email Validation_v3: Validate_Email`). Never add `Email Existence Validator: Check for Disposable emails` on that same address. A separate clause 'is domain X classified as disposable' still gets its own `MailCheck: Domain` call even if X already appeared in an availability clause (X -> `fast Email verifier: FreeDomain` AND `MailCheck: Domain`).

edits.target: A named group or entity search -> the matching `by` field, when the schema offers one (e.g. `Group Name`).
edits.content: A named group or entity search -> the matching `by` field, even when it has a default: 'K-pop girl group Twice' -> `K-POP: girl-groups` with required `q`=`Twice` AND optional `by`=`Group Name`. ENTITY AUDIT: every name, code and date in the clause must land in a field, and codes in parentheses are values too. 'United Airlines (UA) flight 556 from San Francisco (SFO) to Seattle (SEA) on May 25, 2024' on `Flight Info API: schedules` -> optional CarrierCode=`UA`, FlightNumber=`556`, DepartureAirport=`SFO`, ArrivalAirport=`SEA`, DepartureDateTime=`2024-05-25` (five fields, none dropped).

edits.target: When a sibling's name merely contains yours, re-read both descriptions.
edits.content: - GENERIC CLAUSE -> THE SIBLING WHOSE DESCRIPTION REPEATS ITS WORDS. When a provider has per-vertical siblings (hotels / flights / cars) and the clause says only 'travel locations' or 'destinations', take the one whose Description says that (`Priceline com Provider: Search hotels locations`: 'Searches for travel locations by name'), with `name`=`London` and the required type selector `search_type`=`ALL`. The flights sibling ('Searches airports and locations') is only for airport or flight clauses, and the cars sibling only for car rental.

edits.target: Copy values verbatim from the query.
edits.content: - VALUE CASE AND FORM (exception to 'verbatim'). On music tools, category-like values are lowercase: `MusicData API: /youtube/24h/{type}` 'English-language' -> `type`=`english`; `Spotify _v2: New releases` 'in the UK' -> `country`=`uk`; `kjoller: Get songs by composer` 'composed by Bellman' -> `composer`=`bellman`. Artist and group names keep their case (`Twice`, `Halsey`). Airport and airline codes stay uppercase (`SFO`, `UA`). A US state clause on a state-level tool takes the postal code: `Gas Price: stateUsaPrice` 'Washington state' -> `state`=`WA`.
